newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini confident on stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini confident on stability pact deal.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Wednesday he believed a deal on a stability pact for Europe's planned single currency could be reached in time for next week's European Union summit or immediately after it.

"I believe that an accord is still possible for Amsterdam and if it is not possible for Amsterdam, it will be right after," Dini told reporters in parliament. The summit will take place in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17.

France's new Socialist government this week threw the EU's plans for a single currency into confusion by seeking more time to study a previously agreed stability pact to keep budget deficits tight after the currency is launched on January 1 1999.

The pact was supposed to be ratified by EU leaders in Amsterdam at the same time as they approved internal EU reforms in a revised treaty designed to prepare the 15-member bloc for its ambitious expansion eastward.

The European Commission is rushing to find a way to meet France's concerns, which revolve around its view that job creation should play a more important role in the EU's plans for economic and monetary union (EMU).
Dini said intense efforts were under way by all EU member states to try to find a solution in time for Amsterdam.
